question: Can a polynomial system over Z/(2^w), w>=2, have a unique root while its Jacobian at that root has deficient column rank modulo 2?
scope: All word tuples are legal outputs; fixed external inputs; polynomial operations only; not arbitrary bit-vector instructions
finite_check: All ordered pairs of bilinear polynomials c0+c1*x+c2*y+c3*x*y over Z/4 (65536 systems), all 16 possible roots
wide_check: 256 quadratic two-equation systems with a planted i32 root, seed271009; enumerate all four top-bit perturbations
controls: w=1 square has a unique singular root
word rotation is not covered by the polynomial Taylor identity
decision: If rank deficiency forces another legal output, reject singular-Jacobian repair under this scope; do not infer source-code recovery from root evaluation
